newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals turn off early highs.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals turn off early highs.

text.p: Early short covering and a brief rally in the platinum market dissipated around the afternoon gold fixes to leave the precious metals off their intraday highs by mid-afternoon.
"Most of them are still steady with some more consolidation to do but the tone is weaker than it was this morning," a dealer said.
Gold fixed at $345.00 per ounce down a dollar from the morning fixing which had benefited from a short covering rally which reached its peak in the Far East markets.
New York re-opened after the President's Day holiday on Monday to trade in a narrow range and Comex's April contract was $0.20 firmer at $346.90 shortly after the fixing.
The gold price peaked at $346.90 bid earlier aided by firmer platinum and palladium prices which some dealers said was fuelled by buying from Swiss banks.
"Since New York opened, there has been selling from there which has turned the market round," a dealer said.
Platinum was indicated at $366.50/$367.50, up $3.00 from the close but off a high which challenged the psychologically significant $370.00 earlier.
An afternoon challenge of the same level was short lived.

Dealers said this week's statements from Russia -- variously that Norilsk wanted to market its own platinum group metals production -- and that stalled export talks with Japan could start this month or next -- had not greatly hit the price.
"Russia was a factor on the upside. It hasn't been so significant now," a dealer said.
Platinum's premium over gold was around $21.50 this afternoon after widening to around $25.00 earlier.
Dealers said early strength behind platinum reflected spread trades involving buying platinum and selling gold coupled with covering in the Far East and Europe.
Palladium came off its highs by mid-afternoon to be unchanged at $134.00/$135.00 having followed a similar pattern to platinum most of the day.
Silver looked "a bit toppy" at over $5.25 which it struck this morning, dealers said.

By 1600 GMT it has come off the day's low at $5.21 bid to $5.23/$5.25 up three cents. Technically silver looked able to test last August's high of $5.30 after what analysts described as "a constructive bounce".
